steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Sixty percent of the Infected here were infected within the week. They're deteriorating fairly rapidly too.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Almost everyone here seems to have been abusing their Originium Arts. They haven't had time to learn what being an Infected feels like, or how to live as one.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: If only Shining was here... no, even a typical Rhodes Island Medic Operator would be doing a far better job than I am now.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: All I can do is... not enough.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Don't blame yourself, Amiya. You've been at this the whole time.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: There weren't as many Infected in the streets of Norport before. It's true that everyone here fights tooth and nail just to get by, but we are in Londinium after all.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It was only after I had left that I gradually came to realize just how lucky I was. What I took for granted was just exceptions for my privilege.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: People misjudge their own abilities in the environments they inhabit, mistakenly believing they rightfully earned their positions in life through their own efforts.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Only when everything crumbles does one recognize the silver spoon in one's mouth.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Hah. Such self-awareness, Your Royal Highness.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: So, this is what you came back for? To grow a large base of loyalists to help you ascend to the throne?

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Heh, I'm the stupid one here. I actually thought... you were the legendary 'Siege' they would willingly die for.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It was not my intention, Cador.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I've never claimed to be any kind of royalty, but... that move Morgan pulled did prove useful.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You talked of 'unity' before, so regardless, this is just a—

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Wow, such an honor, to earn praise from Her Royal Highness Vina!

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: How touching! Should we shake hands and find your royal photographer to take a picture of us together?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I don't know how I've offended you, Cador, but I believe we should be on the same side.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: The same side?

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Look, you're all clean and innocent... but us?

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Just the other day, we kicked out an old couple.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: They were my neighbors at the apartment I was renting, and they used to be real nice to me, even giving me fried fins they had made too much of.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: When we were dragged out by the Sarkaz and brought to this area, I saw them panicking in the crowd, practically drowning in it, trying their hardest to not let go...

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: I couldn't take it anymore, and I brought them to the boxing gym.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: That old lady worked really hard, and helped us out a ton. The old man... well, he told a good joke, at least, and a night watch with him around was never boring.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: But I had them leave a few days ago.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Delphine gave them two days' worth of rations, and helped them settle down at the Sude Shopping Center's basement car park.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: That place must have already been looted a dozen times, but if you're lucky, you can sometimes find food that's been left behind.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: That's a solid shelter, it should be safe enough.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: But they were Infected. Turned not too long ago at that. I don't know where the Originium dust even floated from, and they're old, and their condition was worsening rapidly.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: And I...

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: I didn't give them a single Oripathy inhibitor. Because they should go to someone younger and stronger who needs it more.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I understand your decision. But...

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: I know. They're ancient. They would probably die from a Sarkaz's Arts, or from a building collapsing in on them, or even from a heart attack triggered by a cannon blast—but I snatched their last shred of hope away from them.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: They might have even survived—but I killed them.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: And I don't think I've done any wrong.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: You know what, Vina? Can you imagine how they were when they left?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I can imagine...

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: No. You can't.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: No crying, no pleading, no cursing. That old man was still making jokes up to the very last moment, mocking the head chef of the old Gaulish restaurant at the mall.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: They clutched their tiny little bag, stuffed with all their remaining hopes. And just like that, they helped each other up through all their shaking and trembling and went out the door.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: If they were unlucky, they might've already been robbed by some roadside lunatic.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: I dreamt of them yesterday.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You're not responsible for any of this, Cador, you're just—

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: You think I dreamt of their tragic deaths? From Oripathy, starvation, or the flames of war? Heh.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: I... I dreamt that the war was over, that Norport had returned to Londinium, and we were rebuilding our home.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: I saw order being restored, the city walls patched up, us living in spanking new houses. And then amongst a crowd celebrating it all, I saw... that old geezer.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Still alive. He had survived, and sometimes it was his wife instead. He or she would stare at me dead-on with those eyes, in the gaps between the fireworks.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: I was never afraid of them dying. I know I made a cruel decision, I forced them to sacrifice themselves for a chance to save some others.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: But what if, when all of this is done and over with, hatred still flows on the peaceful banks of the St. Djuna River? He'll gaze at me, as if asking me—

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: How should I answer? How do I leave this war?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I'm very s—

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Don't apologize, Vina! You don't have the right.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: You hold a sword that only exists in fables, and tell us the former boss of the Glasgow Gang is actually a king, and those young thugs following her are knights, supporters and vassals of royalty—

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: —And then you say, that you've returned, you should help us, you can save us, and we should unite and stand together by your side.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Real funny, innit? After all everyone's been through—

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: After the Glasgow Gang, who helped others run their turf become a ragtag group of drifters, thieves, robbers, and murderers, you've finally returned.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: You became kings, knights, and saints.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: I should be welcoming you with open arms, 'King of the Siege.'

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Your Glasgow Gang isn't here anymore. You are nothing. To us members of the current Glasgow Gang, you are nothing at all.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: But we have to work together!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Only then we can stop—

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: ...survive the war.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: You sure are clever. Vina, we don't plan to stop anything, and you have no good reason for us to sacrifice ourselves for your lofty ideals.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: You lot, and the nobles, are at war with the Sarkaz, fighting over something I could have never thought about my whole life.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: And us utterly defenseless commoners, we're pushed here by just the slightest ripples of your war.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Yes, for the sake of keeping my head. I will first resist the urge to strangle you to death.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: You lot can stay here, and go on with your magnificent plans to save this neighborhood or the whole damned country.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Or you can finish your business, and then leave quietly, just as you arrived.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: I have no thoughts on any of this, 'Your Royal Highness,' am I even qualified to ask?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I'm only a member of the Glasgow Gang, and the Vina you know.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Then we wait and see, Vina.

steps.name: Elderly Sarkaz
steps.text: Phew......
I told you before, Mr. Colbert. Loading up supplies and throwing them out was not a good idea.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: It is indeed different from what I had imagined, Percival.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: I thought... this would somehow help a few people.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: They could have each swiped one of two can of beans, and they could make it last until the next distribution.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: I should have made this even more public—

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: It would have ended the same, Mr. Colbert, or maybe even worse.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Even if they were pretending to be polite before, you should probably hide somewhere safe with the way things are now.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: It's good that you have some life-saving supplies, but take a guess. Would you look more like a saint or a devil in their eyes?

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Haha, I am a Sarkaz, in the first place.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Are they telling the truth?

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: An Aslan heir to the throne? The dukes are following her orders and are about to launch an assault here?

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Hmph, I'm sure you're not one of those street punks who believe in those legends, we all know how the king died.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Whoever they are, they've helped us greatly, so we should...

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Talk with them, right?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Miss Ines! We should gone about this in a gentler...

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: You're the one from before...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Believe us, we mean no harm.

options: We just want to talk to you.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Do you think I'd believe you? A hooded mystery, a Sarkaz mercenary, and your claim of being in cahoots with the Aslan King?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Hmph, anything is possible.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I never expected I'd get another identity for myself here.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: What are you planning?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: You're both from the Sunset Street hotel, right?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Seems like these two know their secret channels well.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: A kindly Sarkaz mercenary gave us some supplies, it's not much, but I think...

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Let's not be hasty, sir. We can talk this out.

options: We also have some attractive proposals for the both of you.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Fine, it doesn't matter who you are, as long as you're serious about helping out Berties.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: So this hotel is still standing... I thought it was a complete ruin from the outside.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: I could spend five hours complaining to you about how difficult it was to put up a facade of ruin.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: We just want to avoid trouble, Mr. Colbert here isn't the fighting sort.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: I hope you won't blame me, but I just want to... maintain the dignity of this hotel.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: It used to be a great place, and I've worked here my whole life, so I couldn't bear to see my hard work burn to ash.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I understand, Mr. Colbert, I remember what it used to look like.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Those dazzling crystal chandeliers, passionate doormen and waiters, and those gorgeous suites.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Not to mention those beautiful flags hanging on the door.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Flags... I see, you were once a valued guest of our establishment.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: That was many years ago.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: We can talk about these things later. I hear there's a Sarkaz mercenary giving you food?

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Yes, a young girl who calls herself Paprika. I have a feeling it's not an easy matter for her.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Paprika?

options: Do you know a mercenary by that name, Ines?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I saw a brief from Ascalon's mission in Highbury, and the name came up.

options: I remember now, she let Catherine go.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Manfred apprehended her, and I thought she was already dead.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: So you're saying this is a genuinely kind Sarkaz?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: No, this means that the food supply is probably within the scope of Manfred's plans.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: The Military Commission needs the people of Norport to stay alive, for now at least.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: What are they waiting for?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: We don't have the time to care about Sarkaz plans now, Rhodes Islanders.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I know this hotel houses a communications station, and I need to use it.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: What are you planning to do?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Contact the dukes, and have them provide backup.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: So, your story about that 'Her Royal Highness' was fake after all.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: You gave the people of Norport a phony promise.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: We're working hard to make it a reality!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: As long as we get a broadcast out, the dukes won't sit idly by. This I can assure you.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: You believe in those nobles that much?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I just believe in their ambition.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: And what about after your broadcast? There's no way to encrypt the frequency here, so the Sarkaz are going to hear it too.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Miss Vina told me that she and the Glasgow Gang will organize an operation to break through the blockade walls, and should they manage it, there should be secret passages leading outside.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: They've used it before.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: So we just have to hold out until the dukes launch their assault.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: And how long will we need to 'hold out?'

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Under four hours.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: You sound certain.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: And after leaving this area? This is a battlefield, after all.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: That's a problem for later. There's no way we can plan for everything in advance.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: We just have to escape this place, and then what happens after will surely...

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Just a second, are there any other guests in the hotel?

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Ah? No, of course not.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: It's just me and Percival hiding here these days.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The shadow is... expanding?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Hide yourself and follow me.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Huh? But—

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Miss Ines, don't drag me!

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Come with me if you want to live, Delphine Windermere!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Wha?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You... how did you...?

options: You'll want to leave here too.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: What? What's going on now?

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Mr. Colbert, do as they say.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}, you...

options: Don't worry, we're still cooperating with him.
You should have a good chat with Miss Delphine.
This is concerning Rhodes Island's future.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: ...I get it.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: No need. I prefer to stand.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: You've gotten me into quite a bit of trouble, Doctor of Rhodes Island. The identity of Her Royal Highness Alexandrina is an extremely sensitive matter in Victoria, and you should have been well aware of this.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I had thought we already came to a tacit understanding on this matter.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: But, well, let us put that aside for the moment...

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Might you introduce me to that hasty blue-haired lady who just left? I would like to make her acquaintance.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Perhaps even share a dance with her.
